meta.title: Lapar Smart: QR Menu Ordering System
meta.author: Abdul Rashid Alias (B24030058)

slides.title: Lapar Smart
slides.subtitle: QR Menu Ordering System for Lazaria Cafe, FAMA
meta: BIT4008 Undergraduate Project, Malaysia University of Science and Technology
slides.notes: Introduce the project: a QR-accessed mobile web application for ordering at the Lazaria Cafe counter. The talk follows the research: literature, problem, evidence, objectives, method, system, testing and conclusion.

slides.title: Three ways a cafe can take orders
slides.lead: The literature review compared the current manual practice with two digital approaches.

cards.head: Manual ordering
cards.text: Orders are given by voice at the counter. It needs no technology, but depends on human accuracy, keeps no record, and shows no progress (Jalaludin et al., 2023).

cards.head: Web menu system
cards.text: Orders are placed in a browser with no app to install, as in the UiTM Tapah and UTHM cafeterias. Browser push alerts are limited (AWS, 2026).

cards.head: QR menu ordering
cards.text: A QR code opens the menu at once. Users find it quick and easy (Shahril et al., 2024), but its value comes from the features behind the code.

slides.notes: Section 2.2.1 to 2.2.3 of the report.

slides.title: Existing systems serve restaurants
slides.note: Research gap: no lightweight system was found that combines a daily menu run by the cafe, meeting-room catering pre-orders, and order tracking with an alert, without a POS subscription.
slides.notes: Sections 2.2.4 to 2.2.6. Not stated means the vendor pages reviewed do not mention the feature.

slides.title: Five problems with ordering at Lazaria Cafe

items.head: Long queues
items.text: The counter is congested at peak hours, so staff lose their short break waiting.

items.head: Wrong orders
items.text: Orders given by voice are misheard, and the wrong food is prepared.

items.head: No order tracking
items.text: Staff wait at the counter because they are not told when the order is ready.

items.head: A menu that changes daily
items.text: The cafe admin has no quick digital way to publish the day's menu.

items.head: Catering by phone
items.text: Meeting-room catering is arranged by phone, so details are delayed or inaccurate.

slides.notes: Section 2.1. The next two slides check these problems with the users.

slides.title: The questionnaire confirms the problems
slides.lead: 30 administrative assistants (Pembantu Tadbir) at FAMA headquarters answered a five-question online form shared through WhatsApp.

stats.label: waited 11 minutes or longer in the queue
received a wrong order at least once
want to pre-order catering for meetings

slides.note: Purposive sample of 30 respondents (Table 3.1 and Appendix D of the report).
slides.notes: 73.3% buy from the cafe three or more times a week, so the queue affects most of them.

slides.title: The cafe admin describes the same problems
slides.lead: A face-to-face interview with the Lazaria Cafe admin, held in Malay on 9 November 2026.

items.head: Daily menu
items.text: The menu is decided every morning from a monthly schedule.

items.head: Counter at lunch time
items.text: The queue is long, and noise makes the admin repeat questions.

items.head: Meeting requests
items.text: They come by phone a day or two ahead, are written on paper, and the headcount often changes.

items.head: Main challenges
items.text: Misheard orders, long queues, knowing who has paid, and keeping track of meeting bookings.

slides.notes: Section 3.2.2 and Appendix A.

slides.title: The findings set four objectives
slides.lead: Aim: a QR-accessed mobile web application for ordering at Lazaria Cafe, FAMA.
columns: Evidence from the questionnaire and interview
rows: 36.7% waited 11 minutes or more; long queues at lunch time
1. Staff scan a QR code, view the daily menu and order from their phone
60.0% got a wrong order; the menu changes every morning
2. An admin module to update the daily menu and the status of each order
93.3% want a notification; staff now wait at the counter
3. An order-ready alert in the app and by email
76.7% want to pre-order; meeting requests are kept on paper
4. Meeting-room catering pre-orders by a Chief Clerk
slides.notes: Objectives from Section 1.2, each traced back to the evidence.

slides.title: Agile Scrum in six sprints over ten weeks
slides.note: One developer acts as product owner, Scrum Master and developer, with a self-review at the end of every sprint.
slides.notes: Scrum leaves room to re-plan after each sprint review.

slides.title: From requirements to a tested design

cards.head: Data collection
cards.text: A questionnaire for FAMA staff and an interview with the cafe admin set the requirements.

cards.head: UML modelling
cards.text: Use case, sequence, class, entity relationship, architecture and data flow diagrams.

cards.head: Requirements
cards.text: 15 functional and 4 non-functional requirements, each linked to a use case.

cards.head: Testing method
cards.text: A functional test and a regression test for every one of the 14 use cases.

slides.notes: Sections 3.2 to 3.4.

slides.title: Three kinds of user, fourteen use cases

cards.head: FAMA Staff
cards.text: Scan the QR code, browse the menu, place a counter order and track it. No login.

cards.head: Chief Clerk (CC)
cards.text: Registers and logs in with a Staff ID to order meeting-room catering.

cards.head: Cafe Admin
cards.text: Manages the daily menu, orders, order status and Cafe Admin accounts.

slides.notes: The Chief Clerk is a specialisation of FAMA Staff in the use case diagram.

slides.title: A three-tier architecture on free cloud tiers

points.head: Email
points.text: Gmail SMTP for alerts and resets

slides.notes: Turso replaced a local SQLite file because the Vercel file system is not persistent.

slides.title: Staff order from their phone in three steps
bullets: Scan the QR code. The daily menu opens with no login.
Choose items and quantities from today's menu.
Review the order and enter Staff ID, name, department, phone and email.
The server re-reads every price, so the browser is never trusted.
slides.notes: Objective 1. Use cases Scan QR Code, View Daily Menu, Place Order and Review Order.

slides.title: The order is tracked until it is ready
bullets: Four statuses: Pending, Preparing, Ready and Completed.
The status page refreshes every 3 seconds and shows an alert at Ready.
An email is sent through Gmail, so the alert arrives even when the page is closed.
Payment is made at the counter on collection.
slides.notes: Objective 3. Use case Receive Order Notification.

slides.title: Chief Clerks reserve catering for meeting rooms
bullets: The Meeting Order button leads to the Chief Clerk login.
Each package lists its food and its beverages by the jug.
The Chief Clerk chooses the room, the date and time, and the quantity.
An email follows at Pending, Preparing, Ready and Completed.
At Ready, cafe staff deliver the order to the meeting room.
slides.notes: Objective 4. Use case Reserve Meeting Room Order.

slides.title: The cafe admin runs the day from one dashboard
bullets: View and filter counter and meeting-room orders.
Move an order to the next status with one click.
Add, hide or delete items on the daily menu.
Manage Cafe Admin accounts, with registration and password reset by email.
slides.notes: Objective 2. Use cases View Orders, Update Order Status, Mark Order Completed, Update Daily Menu and Manage Cafe Admins.

slides.title: Every use case passed its tests
slides.note: Each test was run through the user interface on the final build and compared with its expected output (Chapter 5 and Appendix C).
slides.notes: FT is the functional test and RT the regression test of each use case.

slides.title: Every objective is achieved
rows: Scan QR Code, View Daily Menu, Place Order, Review Order
Update Daily Menu, View Orders, Update Order Status, Mark Completed, Manage Admins, Register, Forgot Password, Login
slides.note: Objective 3 is achieved with an in-app alert, shown while the status page is open, and an email alert (Table 5.5 of the report).
slides.notes: Each objective is traced to its use cases, requirements and test cases.
slides.lead: The traceability matrix links each objective to its use cases, requirements and test cases.

slides.title: Strengths of the system

items.head: Ordering from a phone
items.text: Staff order without queuing at the counter.

items.head: Alerts that reach staff
items.text: An in-app alert and an email when the order is ready.

items.head: One dashboard
items.text: The admin updates the daily menu and every order status in one place.

items.head: Meeting-room catering
items.text: Chief Clerks pre-order packages instead of phoning the cafe.

slides.notes: Section 6.1.

slides.title: Limitations of the system

items.head: Payment at the counter
items.text: No online or e-wallet payment is built in.

items.head: No user acceptance test
items.text: Usability has not yet been confirmed by FAMA staff.

items.head: Self-reported identity
items.text: Staff details and Chief Clerk registration are not verified.

items.head: In-app alert needs the page open
items.text: The email alert covers the case when the page is closed.

items.head: Load tested locally only
items.text: High order volumes were not tested on the production database.

slides.notes: Section 6.2.

slides.title: Future work

cards.head: Online payment
cards.text: Add an e-wallet or payment gateway so staff can pay in the app.

cards.head: Verified identity
cards.text: Check staff identity and approve Chief Clerk registrations.

cards.head: Push alerts
cards.text: Deliver alerts with Web Push or as a Progressive Web App.

cards.head: User acceptance test
cards.text: Test with FAMA staff and run a production-scale load test.

slides.notes: Section 6.3.

slides.title: Scan, Order & Enjoy
slides.subtitle: Scan the QR code or open the link to try Lapar Smart.
slides.notes: Open the production site for the live demonstration.
